description: The image is a false-colour satellite or aerial photograph depicting an area of diverse agricultural land. It primarily shows numerous small, irregularly-shaped to rectangular land parcels, characteristic of "complex cultivation patterns." These parcels display a mix of colours: bright reds (indicating healthy vegetation in false-colour infrared), various shades of green/teal, and lighter grey/brown areas, suggesting different crop types, stages of growth, or bare soil. A prominent, dark red linear feature, likely a canal or a road, runs diagonally from the top-right to the middle-right of the image. A thin, yellow-green line delineates a larger area encompassing many of these small, diverse parcels. In the top-left corner, some grey features with linear patterns suggest built-up areas or infrastructure. The image illustrates the visual appearance of agricultural parcels, often covering less than 0.5 ha, that are mixed with rows of trees or vines, contributing to a coarse texture and diverse colour palette, as described for the "complex cultivation patterns" land cover class in Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) guidelines.
